title: Echo Observatory · Operations
description: Portable operational dashboard for Echo Observatory 2.x. Standard Grafana panels and Prometheus only; no provider-specific metrics or plugins.

panels.title: Operations overview
panels.description: Start with readiness and demand; expand protocol, protection and runtime sections for diagnostics.

options.content:
### Your service, at a glance
Health, demand and resource use across every listener. Filter by **Job**, **Instance** or **Listener**. Demand excludes admin traffic. Expand the sections below for protocol, protection and runtime details.

Use **Inspect → Data** on any chart for a table or CSV. Empty panels show unavailable or not-yet-observed metrics, never fabricated zeroes.

panels.title: Readiness
panels.description: Ready instances / selected instances with readiness samples. This is not a scrape-availability check; inspect Scrape health below.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Completed echo/UI HTTP requests, TCP sessions and gRPC calls. Admin traffic excluded; long-lived sessions count when they finish. This is not a visitor count.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Estimated increase over the selected interval, adjusted for counter resets. Streaming sessions count at completion; not unique users.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Physical accepted transport connections. WebSocket logical sessions excluded to avoid double counting. Admin connections excluded.

panels.title: Egress rate
panels.description: Successfully sent socket bytes, including TLS/QUIC framing. Not provider-billed traffic: excludes network headers, retransmissions and infrastructure traffic.

panels.title: Process RAM
panels.description: Resident memory summed across selected processes. Includes the Go heap and other process memory, not total VM/container usage.

panels.title: Demand by listener
panels.description: Completed operations per second. WebSocket and streaming RPCs count at the end of the session. Listener filter applies.

panels.title: HTTP handler latency
panels.description: Combined HTTP p50 / p95, in seconds. Includes configured demo delays and unsuccessful outcomes. Excludes admin, raw TCP, WebSocket sessions and gRPC lifetimes. Sparse traffic makes percentiles approximate.

panels.title: HTTP outcomes
panels.description: Actual HTTP statuses, including intentionally requested errors; 4xx/5xx do not necessarily indicate application faults. Canceled/panic outcomes have no final status. Admin excluded.

panels.title: Application failures & rejected work
panels.description: Internal application failures and admission rejections are separate from deliberate test statuses. No samples means no matching event series yet. Listener filter applies.

panels.title: Liveness & readiness
panels.description: Per instance. 1 = healthy/ready, 0 = unhealthy/not ready. A missing scrape is a gap, not a healthy zero. Listener selection does not apply.

panels.title: Scrape health
panels.description: Prometheus up: 1 = last scrape succeeded, 0 = failed. Restricted to targets with Echo readiness samples in the selected range. No match is not healthy. Some managed stores do not publish scrape metadata.

panels.title: Configured listener state
panels.description: 1 = running, 0 = stopped. Disabled listeners have no series. H2C is the shared HTTP/1.1 + h2c server when enabled; it is not a second physical HTTP listener.

panels.title: Connections & logical sessions
panels.description: Transport connections by listener. WebSocket is a separate logical session category over HTTP/TLS: compare the lines, do not sum them.

panels.title: Work in flight
panels.description: Running HTTP handlers and gRPC calls, including upgraded WebSocket and streaming lifetimes. Not queued work. Admin excluded.

panels.title: Route activity
panels.description: Rates by bounded route label, never raw URLs or query strings. Arbitrary echo paths share other. Includes the UI; admin excluded.

panels.title: New connections
panels.description: Accepted connections per second; compare transport and logical WebSocket lines independently to avoid double counting.

panels.title: HTTP latency by listener
panels.description: p95 handler duration by HTTP listener. Excludes admin, raw TCP, gRPC and WebSocket session lifetimes. Includes configured demo delays.

panels.title: TCP session duration
panels.description: p50/p95 duration of native TCP metadata sessions. This includes writing the response and closing, not network round-trip latency.

panels.title: HTTP protocol adoption
panels.description: Completed HTTP requests by negotiated protocol. Includes UI requests, excludes admin; not unique connections.

panels.title: IPv4 & IPv6 request activity
panels.description: HTTP requests by observed client IP family. No addresses are stored in these labels. This is request activity, not unique visitors.

panels.title: HTTP response bodies
panels.description: HTTP body bytes only, excluding headers, encryption and WebSocket frames. Compare with the transport chart below; do not add the two measurements.

panels.title: Transport throughput
panels.description: Socket traffic by listener and direction, including TLS/QUIC framing. Excludes IP/TCP/UDP headers, retransmissions and infrastructure traffic; not a billing meter.

panels.title: Transport data in range
panels.description: Estimated sent / received bytes over the selected time range, adjusted for counter resets. Admin excluded; not billed data.

panels.title: gRPC outcomes
panels.description: Completed unary/streaming RPCs by method and final status, including echo, health and reflection. Listener selection does not apply: these series have no listener label.

panels.title: gRPC call & session lifetime
panels.description: p50/p95 seconds by RPC method. Streaming values include the entire session and are not per-message latency. Listener selection does not apply.

panels.title: WebSocket messages
panels.description: Complete text/binary messages received and echoed; control frames excluded. Listener selection does not apply: WebSocket counters have direction/type labels only.

panels.title: WebSocket payload throughput
panels.description: Message payload bytes; excludes WebSocket framing and control traffic. Compare sent/received, not total transport bytes. Listener selection does not apply.

panels.title: Protection configuration
panels.description: Per instance: enabled, persistent reservations and daily allowance. 0 enabled = protection disabled; 0 persistent = in-memory accounting. Job/Instance filters apply; Listener does not.

panels.title: Daily allowance remaining
panels.description: Per protected instance, for its current UTC budget day. 100% = unreserved allowance intact. Reservations can exceed bytes actually sent; restarts may lose unused leases. Each replica has its own budget. Not a provider billing cap.

panels.title: Reserved & unreserved bytes
panels.description: Current UTC budget day, not the dashboard interval. Disabled protection is omitted. Durable reservations are charged before all bytes are sent and survive restart.

panels.title: Rejected work by listener
panels.description: Rejected operations/connections, grouped by bounded reason. No samples means no rejection series yet; waiting for capacity is backpressure, not a rejection.

panels.title: Operation & connection headroom
panels.description: Fraction of global burst tokens currently available. 100% = full; near 0% = little burst capacity. Sampled snapshots can miss short bursts; rejection counters retain them. Limits are per process, shared across listeners.

panels.title: Transfer headroom
panels.description: Remaining ingress/egress burst capacity, in percent. Refills at the configured bytes/second rate. This is short-term rate capacity, separate from the daily allowance.

panels.title: Charged operations & sustained limits
panels.description: Solid lines: global tokens consumed per second; dashed: configured refill. Operations include HTTP requests, RPCs and WebSocket messages. Connections are charged before expensive handshakes and may later fail peer admission. Bursts can temporarily exceed refill.

panels.title: Charged bytes & sustained limits
panels.description: Solid: ingress received / egress reserved bytes per second. Dashed: configured refill. Reservations are conservative and can exceed successfully sent bytes. Bursts can exceed refill temporarily; not billed traffic.

panels.title: Peer headroom · lowest observed
panels.description: Minimum token fraction across client groups seen in the last 10 minutes. Each line may represent a different group over time. 100% when no recent groups remain; unavailable when peer limits are disabled. No addresses or identities are exported.

panels.title: Peer tracking capacity
panels.description: Recently active IPv4 address / IPv6 /64 groups divided by the bounded 4096-entry capacity. Inactive groups are ignored at scrape time. Near capacity, LRU eviction can reset a peer burst; tune protection with this in mind.

panels.title: Global bucket rejections
panels.description: Insufficient global tokens, by bucket. Counts failed admission attempts, not rejected bytes. Excludes peer limits, concurrency caps and daily quota; use the rejection-reasons chart for the complete view.

panels.title: Configured rate & burst
panels.description: Per instance and bucket. Operations/connections use tokens; ingress/egress use bytes. Peer values apply to each client group. No rate metrics are exported when protection is disabled.

panels.title: Time to expiry
panels.description: Minimum remaining validity across selected instances, based on the last ordinary server leaf certificate observed. Negative means expired. Not a renewal-success guarantee. No samples until a certificate is observed or when running a version without certificate metrics.

panels.title: Earliest expiry
panels.description: Expiry date of the last observed ordinary certificate, across selected instances. Uses client-local display time. Leaf expiry alone does not verify the trust chain, hostname or renewal service.

panels.title: Valid from
panels.description: Most recent validity start across selected instances. A future time means the certificate is not yet valid. ACME challenge certificates are excluded.

panels.title: Certificate validity remaining
panels.description: Seconds to leaf expiry per instance. An upward step after a handshake is consistent with a renewed certificate being selected. The same shared certificate serves HTTPS, TLS gRPC and HTTP/3. Values do not identify the issuer and do not prove trust or future renewal.

panels.title: Resident memory & Go heap
panels.description: RSS, live heap and heap reserved from the OS, per process. These overlap: do not sum the lines. Does not include the host OS or other processes. Listener selection does not apply.

panels.title: Process CPU · one core = 100%
panels.description: CPU fraction of one core: 100% = one full core. This is process CPU, not host CPU quota or throttling; multiple cores can exceed 100%. Listener selection does not apply.

panels.title: Goroutines & OS threads
panels.description: Counts per process. Sustained growth without matching traffic may merit investigation; no universal threshold is assumed.

panels.title: GC frequency & pause
panels.description: GC cycles per second on the left axis; mean stop-the-world pause per GC on the right. Empty pause series means no observed GC during that interval.

targets.expr: (rate(go_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) and on(job, instance) max_over_time(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) / (rate(go_gc_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) and on(job, instance) max_over_time(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Process uptime
panels.description: Seconds since process start, per instance. Resets on restart; this is not service availability over the selected period.

panels.title: File descriptor use
panels.description: Open descriptors divided by the process limit, where supported by the operating system. A missing series is unavailable, not zero. High sustained use can indicate connection pressure or leaked files.

targets.expr: (process_open_fds{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} and on(job, instance) max_over_time(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) / clamp_min((process_max_fds{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} and on(job, instance) max_over_time(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])), 1)

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Prometheus scrape duration, where the datasource publishes it. No samples means unavailable, not a zero-cost scrape. Listener selection does not apply.

panels.title: Exporter errors
panels.description: Exporter metric gathering/encoding errors per second, where available. No samples is not a zero-error guarantee; also inspect Scrape health.

panels.title: Dependency readiness
panels.description: Only exists when an external readiness dependency is configured. 1 = ready, 0 = pending/failing. No samples normally means no dependency is configured.

panels.title: Background probe results
panels.description: Actual background checks by result. Scraping and readiness requests do not trigger additional outbound checks.

panels.title: Background probe latency
panels.description: p95 duration of actual dependency checks, in seconds. No samples when no probe is configured or no checks have been observed.
